heard: The famous pigeon hero of World War, I may have been misidentified. On October 4, 1918, the Lost Battalion was trapped in the Argonne Forest under heavy fire. Major Charles Whittlesey wrote an urgent message asking to stop the friendly fire barrage. Private Omer Richards released Cher Ami into the smoke-filled air to carry the plea. The brave bird flew 25 miles in just 25 minutes back to division headquarters. During that dangerous flight, Sher Ami was shot in the chest and nearly lost a leg. Smithsonian curator Frank Blaesich notes official records show the wounding happened on a different mission entirely. DNA analysis also proved the bird was male despite early Signal Corps records listing him as a hen. Military records suggest the legendary pigeon's biggest flight was actually a different bird.
